title: Foraminiferal forms follow such simple laws that none is fitter than another to survive

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Foraminiferal forms follow such simple laws that none is fitter than another to survive

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Foraminiferal shells grow by laws so simple and so in harmony with their material and the forces acting on them that no form is better, fitter or less fit to survive than another, which accounts for the great diversity of types and their persistence since the Cretaceous.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XII: The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It leads one to imagine that these shells have grown according to laws so simple, so much in harmony with their material, with their environment, and with all the forces internal and external to which they are exposed, that none is better than another and none fitter or less fit to survive.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XII, “The Spiral Shells of the Foraminifera”; topic “Conclusion: evolution of foraminiferal form”. Scope: Foraminifera

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch12-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.39

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A restricted trait-dependent survival test is possible, but it captures only one meaning of fitness. The universal equality and proposed explanation are too broad to resolve cleanly with observational datasets.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define fitness as lineage persistence or extinction risk and test whether shell-form traits predict survival across environmental transitions in fossil occurrence data. Detectable trait-dependent survival would refute the equal-fitness assertion, while no association under well-powered models would only weakly support it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Preservation and sampling strongly confound form-dependent survival.

'Simple laws' and fitness are not uniquely defined.

Fossil persistence is a noisy proxy for organismal fitness.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is an inference about fitness from the simplicity of the growth laws, and fitness is not a column in any foraminiferal archive. Ranges and census counts can show whether some shell forms are markedly less persistent or less common than others, which is a partial empirical shadow of the claim. Those proxies would not isolate 'none fitter than another' from sampling bias or from selection that does not change durations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use stratigraphic durations and relative abundances of foraminiferal morphotypes as proxies for persistence and commonness, and ask whether shell-form classes differ in those proxies after sampling correction. Equal fitness would look like indistinguishable durations and abundances across forms; large, repeated differences would count against the claim, without identifying the selective cause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stratigraphic range and abundance are weak stand-ins for fitness and are dominated by preservation and sampling.

Equal persistence is compatible with neutral coexistence, fluctuating selection, and many forms of weak selection.
